explanations.answer: He keeps watch with His own eyes
explanations.explanation: That's the reason in the verse, baker. The LORD says, “…never again will an oppressor overrun My people, for now I keep watch with My own eyes.” (Zechariah 9:8). The promise rests on the LORD watching with His own eyes. The verse gives no other reason.

explanations.answer: Their walls will be too high
explanations.explanation: Walls feel like a natural reason, but the verse doesn't use it. Speaking of His people, the LORD says, “…for now I keep watch with My own eyes.” (Zechariah 9:8). Remember Tyre and her fortress, because this promise doesn't depend on walls.

explanations.answer: Their army will be too strong
explanations.explanation: The verse does mention an army, so I see the pull. But the reason given is something else. The LORD says, “…for now I keep watch with My own eyes.” (Zechariah 9:8). The promise isn't based on how strong their army is.

After all that burden talk, you'd expect more bad news. But verse 9 turns the mood right around. “Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion! Shout in triumph, O Daughter of Jerusalem!” (Zechariah 9:9). They're told to rejoice and shout in triumph.

Moab is a name you'll find elsewhere in the Bible, but it isn't in this verse. The LORD says, “I will rouse your sons, O Zion, against the sons of Greece.” (Zechariah 9:13). The sons are Zion's sons.
Edom turns up in other places in Scripture, but not in this one. The verse says, “I will rouse your sons, O Zion, against the sons of Greece.” (Zechariah 9:13). The answer here is Zion.

A wall of bronze would be solid, no question. But the verse picks a weapon, not a wall. The LORD says, “I will make you like the sword of a mighty man.” (Zechariah 9:13). It's a sword.
